title: Progressive traffic steering and session-affinity reconciliation for active-active streaming handoff
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers use long-lived streaming connections and sessionful chat flows. During region-level capacity pressure or partial outages we must shift traffic between regions without truncating in-flight streams, violating latency SLOs, or causing mass reconnect storms. Current approach (hard cutover + circuit-based fallback) results in abrupt stream terminations and an inconsistent session cache state that complicates resumption.

Goal: Implement a progressive steering and session-affinity reconciliation mechanism that lets the edge perform gradual traffic shifts while preserving stream continuity or providing a resumable handoff path with clear SLO behavior and bounded customer impact. The design must integrate edge-side circuit breakers and probabilistic load-shedding so we maintain p95 latency and error-rate SLOs during shifts and scale events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Edge can perform percent-based steering for a given customer route with 0.1% granularity and observe per-customer in-flight session counts in real time. 2) Active streaming sessions that are routed away during a progressive shift either continue without interruption (preferred) or reconnect and resume from within one token-chunk (<= 2s of content) for >= 95% of sessions. 3) No increase > 2x in reconnect storms during rollouts compared to baseline. 4) Circuit breaker triggers and load-shedding decisions are visible in Console with per-route impact breakdown. 5) Runbook and rollback path validated in canary region and staging before cross-region rollout.
technical_notes:
Core components: 1) Edge routing: extend existing gateway router to support 'progressive steering policies' (percentage windows, warm-up cooldown) and to issue ephemeral session_handshake tokens attached as connection metadata. 2) Session metadata store: lightweight, strongly-consistent write path to replication ring (multi-region write quorum) for a short TTL (default 30s) to allow dual-region ownership during handoff. 3) Streaming resume protocol: include resume_token + last_emitted_offset; runtime will attempt to fetch prefix cache or tokenized snapshot to continue generation. 4) Circuit/backpressure: per-edge per-route circuit state machine with three thresholds: warn (latency > p95_target), shed (queued_req_count > threshold), and open (error-rate > threshold). Backpressure policy uses probabilistic shedding by request weight plus explicit reject-with-retry-after for non-streaming. 5) KV prefix replication: replicate only last N tokens (configurable, default 64 tokens) to warm standby to reduce cold-resume costs. 6) Telemetry: new metrics: steering_percent, in_flight_sessions, resume_success_ratio, shed_rate_by_route, circuit_state_gauge. Logs must include session_token, src_region, dest_region, and decision_reason.

Trade-offs and notes: - Stronger consistency (multi-write) increases write latency; mitigate by making TTL short and using async amplify for non-critical fields. - Full prefix replication for all sessions is costly; we limit to hot sessions and leaky bucket heuristics. - Resume protocol relies on both runtime and client supporting resume_token; where client support is absent, fall back to user-visible reconnect with short truncation notice.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): implement router + token handshake + metrics; smoke tests for resume protocol with internal clients. Phase 2 (canary): enable progressive steering for a single low-risk customer in us-west with 1% steps up to 20% across 48 hours, observe resume_success_ratio and shed_rate. Phase 3 (regional): enable for multiple routes with feature flag per-customer; monitor for reconnect storms and latency regressions. Phase 4 (global): enable defaults and runbook publishing. Each phase includes an explicit abort condition: resume_success_ratio < 90% or surge in reconnects > 2x baseline or circuit.open_count increases by 50% for 10m.

Rollback steps: disable steering flag and revert to existing sticky routing; instruct edge to drain in-flight sessions to origin region for remaining TTL and reject new handoff requests.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Console -> Active-Active Steering (new) with widgets for steering_percent, resume_success_ratio (p50/p95), in_flight_sessions_by_region, shed_rate_by_customer. Alerts: P1 if resume_success_ratio < 90% for >5m or shed_rate_by_route > 0.1 for >10m. Pager policy: on-call infra + serving runtime. Create Grafana link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/active-active-steer (placeholder).
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for router policy evaluation, integration tests for token handshake and resume replay, chaos test: simulated region drop while 1k concurrent streams active to validate graceful reconnect percentage. Load test matrix: streaming session lengths 2s/30s/5m, percent steering steps 1/5/20/50. Post-deployment validation: synthetic canary agent executes reconnect/resume scenarios and reports telemetry to infra dashboard. GitHub PR for initial implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1229 (prototype).
runbook_snippets: If resume_success_ratio drops below threshold: 1) Pause current steering rollout (feature flag). 2) Inspect edge circuit state and per-route shed_rate for hotspots. 3) If shed_rate concentrated on specific customers, throttle that customer's steering or reduce steer_percent. 4) If circuit.open_count rising across multiple edges, disable steering globally and allow regional failover path. 5) Coordinate with traffic engineering to reverse BGP shifts only if needed.

notes_for_reviewers: Key review areas: 1) latency impact of short-lived multi-write for session metadata and whether we should instead use async replication with optimistic reads. 2) Circuit threshold defaults and their interaction with current global autoscaling. 3) Security: ensure resume_token cannot be replayed cross-customer; token includes HMAC with route-scoped key. Please comment on the proposed defaults and any additional telemetry required.
